result.summary: The street features sidewalks on both sides, though the right walkway is partially obstructed by utility poles. There is a lack of marked pedestrian crossings or traffic calming measures, and the presence of blank building frontages reduces natural surveillance.

hazards.name: Sidewalk Obstructions
hazards.description: Utility poles are located within the clear path of the right-side sidewalk, creating obstacles for pedestrians, especially those with mobility aids.

hazards.name: Lack of Marked Crossings
hazards.description: No marked crosswalks are visible at the approaching intersection, which may lead to unpredictable pedestrian movements and reduced driver awareness.

hazards.name: Blank Frontage
hazards.description: The long, windowless red wall on the right creates a lack of 'eyes on the street,' which can decrease the perceived and actual safety of pedestrians.

interventions.title: High-Visibility Crosswalks
interventions.description: Install continental-style marked crosswalks at the intersection to clearly define pedestrian space.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Add curb extensions at the intersection to shorten crossing distances and improve sightlines between drivers and pedestrians.

interventions.title: Sidewalk Clear Zone Maintenance
interventions.description: Relocate or consolidate utility poles to ensure a continuous, unobstructed clear path for pedestrians.

result.summary: The image shows a wide, continuous concrete sidewalk in front of a multi-story brick residential building. While the walkway is spacious, there is no physical buffer or greenery separating pedestrians from the adjacent roadway.

hazards.name: Lack of pedestrian buffer
hazards.description: There is no physical separation, such as trees or a planting strip, between the wide sidewalk and the travel lane.
hazards.location_in_image: Along the curb line at the bottom of the frame

hazards.name: Litter and debris
hazards.description: Loose trash on the sidewalk surface could present a minor tripping hazard or indicate poor maintenance.
hazards.location_in_image: On the sidewalk surface in the foreground

interventions.title: Street Trees and Planters
interventions.description: Installing street trees or large planters would provide a vertical buffer between pedestrians and vehicles while improving the microclimate.

interventions.title: Pedestrian-Scale Lighting
interventions.description: Adding street lamps would improve visibility and perceived safety for pedestrians at night.

result.summary: The image shows a narrow urban residential street with sidewalks on both sides and parallel parking. While the narrow street width naturally limits vehicle speeds, the environment lacks marked pedestrian crossings, traffic calming measures, and has some sidewalk obstructions like trash bins.

hazards.name: Sidewalk Obstructions
hazards.description: Trash bins and debris are located on the sidewalk, narrowing the effective walking path.

hazards.name: Lack of Marked Crossings
hazards.description: There are no visible marked crosswalks at the intersection or mid-block, forcing pedestrians to cross in unmarked areas.

hazards.name: Visual Obstructions from Parked Cars
hazards.description: Continuous parallel parking on both sides of the narrow street can obscure pedestrians from the view of approaching drivers.

interventions.title: High-Visibility Crosswalks
interventions.description: Install continental-style marked crosswalks at the intersection to clearly define pedestrian right-of-way.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Implement curb extensions (bulb-outs) at intersections to shorten crossing distances and improve sightlines between drivers and pedestrians.

interventions.title: Speed Humps
interventions.description: Install speed humps to physically enforce low vehicle speeds on this residential street.

result.summary: The pedestrian environment consists of a continuous, well-maintained sidewalk directly fronting residential rowhouses. Safety is limited by the lack of a buffer between the walkway and the adjacent parallel parking lane, which creates visual obstructions. No traffic calming measures or pedestrian-oriented infrastructure like street trees are visible in this mid-block section.

hazards.name: Visual Obstruction
hazards.description: Parked vehicles along the curb block sight lines between the sidewalk and the travel lane, which is hazardous for mid-block crossings.
